llm.summary: This website-building skill is not clearly malicious, but it should be reviewed because its generated auth, payment, analytics, and deployment code does not consistently match its production-security claims.

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose, a full-stack EdgeOne Pages website generator with auth, payments, AI chat, analytics, admin tools, and deployment, is coherent, but those capabilities are high-impact and several implemented security controls are incomplete or contradicted by runtime code.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md includes useful confirmation checkpoints before deployment, secrets, database migration, payment activation, and code generation, but README/metadata still advertise one-sentence automatic deployment and broad triggers that can start sensitive workflows from generic website requests.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No hidden install hook or automatic privilege escalation was found; scripts are manual and mostly scaffold, sync, or publish files. The workflow does ask users to install and log into the EdgeOne CLI and can write local env files when run.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Payment keys, JWT secrets, database access, AI API keys, public deployment, and analytics are proportionate to the advertised app, but the generated code exposes tokens to JavaScript, auto-runs analytics without a consent gate, and has misleading payment/auth safety claims.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill creates persistent sessions, refresh-token metadata, analytics records, chat history, order data, cron transitions, and deployed public endpoints. Persistence is disclosed, but token/session handling and analytics persistence are under-controlled for production use.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Treat this skill as experimental scaffolding, not production-ready infrastructure. Before installing or using it with real users, real payment credentials, production secrets, or a live deployment, review and fix the auth, token storage, payment callback verification, idempotency, analytics consent, and secret-handling paths. Keep deployment, database migration, cron, and payment activation behind explicit user approval.
llm.findings:
[SDI-4] unexpected: Accepted in part: artifact text claims JWT middleware and HttpOnly-cookie auth, but _middleware.js only passes requests onward, and login/refresh return access and refresh tokens in JSON responses while the frontend stores tokens in localStorage.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Accepted in part: the payment package's verifyPayment placeholder returns valid for any parseable JSON body, which conflicts with the skill's production-grade payment verification claims.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Accepted in part: create-order.js claims a KV idempotency lock but does not enforce one, and logout.js can act on a client-supplied sessionId before strongly binding the request to the authenticated caller.
[SQP-1] expected: Downgraded but relevant: broad website-building triggers are expected for this category, and SKILL.md has confirmation checkpoints, but the deployment and payment scope should be more explicit at invocation time.
[SQP-2] expected: Accepted in part: deployment, secrets, AI calls, notifications, and analytics are expected features, but analytics auto-initializes with persistent identifiers and lacks a visible consent/minimization gate.
[SQP-3] expected: Downgraded: browser language collection is low-risk alone, but it compounds with user/session IDs, URL path, referrer, and screen data in the analytics payload.
